title: Malicious inbox rule creation preceded by an anomalous sign-in
event_type: Mailbox-audit event (New-InboxRule) joined with the preceding sign-in event for the same mailbox, illustrating the DET-17-04 / HUNT-17-02 join

fields.label: SignInLocation / ASN
fields.value: Lagos, NG — AS29465 (no prior sign-in history for this mailbox)

fields.label: ClientAppUsed
fields.value: generic OAuth API client (not the standard web mail-client UI)

callouts.explanation: The rule is created only five minutes after the sign-in — this is the join HUNT-17-02 relies on: a rule-creation event is far higher confidence when it follows a sign-in anomaly by minutes rather than appearing with no correlated sign-in context at all.

A new ASN/geo with no prior sign-in history for this mailbox is the sign-in-side anomaly Part 12's identity telemetry would flag; on its own it's only low-to-medium confidence, per §9's discussion of composite BEC chains.

An external domain not in KnownOrgDomains is the core signal DET-17-04's query filters on; this is the field the ForwardTo/RedirectTo/ForwardAsAttachmentTo coalesce in the KQL sample is trying to populate.

DeleteMessage = True is the evidence-hiding action that escalates this from a plain external-forward alert to the higher-severity tier described in the Detection Autopsy for DET-17-04 — it removes the victim's own copy of the forwarded mail.

note: This is a conceptual, illustrative field breakdown built to match the prose discussion of DET-17-04 and HUNT-17-02 — not a captured screenshot, and no product interface is depicted; the author's lab has no mail-tenant infrastructure to generate this telemetry organically.
